column1: Why must an entity maintain adequate sustainability records under section 286A of the Corporations Act?
column2: Records must be kept to explain and substantiate all methods, assumptions, and evidence used to prepare the sustainability report.

column1: Under section 292A(2) of the Corporations Act, what reporting choice does a parent entity have regarding group boundaries?
column2: A parent entity may choose whether to prepare its sustainability report for the consolidated group or for the parent entity alone.

column1: How must a reporting entity align its climate disclosure boundary with its related financial statements under paragraph Aus20.1?
column2: The climate-related financial disclosures must represent the exact same reporting entity as the related financial statements unless permitted by law.

column1: Why was mandatory climate-related financial reporting introduced in Australia?
column2: It was introduced to improve the quality, consistency, and comparability of climate disclosures so investors can make informed decisions.

column1: How is a shadow carbon price used within internal corporate planning?
column2: A shadow price is a theoretical cost used internally to evaluate economic trade-offs and project investment risks without charging actual fees.

column1: What is the minimum number of climate scenarios an entity must use when performing climate-related scenario analysis?
column2: Entities must use a minimum of two climate scenarios referable to temperature targets set out in the Climate Change Act 2022.

column1: What modified standard applies to the directors' declaration for financial years commencing between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2027?
column2: Directors declare that the entity took reasonable steps to ensure the report complies with the Corporations Act and AASB S2.

column1: What defines Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions under AASB S2?
column2: Scope 3 emissions are indirect greenhouse gas emissions occurring throughout an entity's upstream and downstream value chain, excluding Scope 2 emissions.

column1: What primary criteria under Chapter 2M of the Corporations Act require an entity to prepare a sustainability report?
column2: An entity must be required to prepare an annual financial report under Chapter 2M and meet a sustainability reporting threshold under section 292A.

column1: What are the threshold criteria for non-RSE corporate entities to enter Group 2 sustainability reporting?
column2: Entities must meet two of three criteria: revenue of $200 million or more, gross assets of $500 million or more, or 250 or more employees.

column1: Under what condition can ASIC grant individual relief from statutory sustainability reporting requirements?
column2: ASIC can grant prospective relief for up to 12 months if statutory jurisdictional thresholds under section 342(1) are met.

column1: What is the statutory lodgement deadline for disclosing entities and registered schemes submitting sustainability reports to ASIC?
column2: Sustainability reports must be lodged within three months after the end of the financial year.

column1: What must an entity disclose if it omits quantitative financial effect disclosures due to high uncertainty or resource constraints?
column2: It must explain the omission, provide qualitative financial impacts, identify affected statement line items, and state combined effects where useful.

column1: What is the primary objective of the metrics and targets pillar in AASB S2?
column2: It enables users to understand an entity's performance regarding climate risks and opportunities and its progress toward set targets.

column1: What information must an entity disclose regarding planned carbon credit usage for net emissions targets?
column2: The entity must disclose its reliance extent, verifying scheme, credit type, offset mechanism, and factors proving credibility and permanence.

column1: How many categories of Scope 3 emissions are specified under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Value Chain Standard?
column2: The GHG Protocol specifies 15 distinct categories of Scope 3 emissions.

column1: Which default accounting standard must entities use to measure greenhouse gas emissions under AASB S2?
column2: Entities must measure emissions using the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (2004) unless jurisdictional authorities require otherwise.

column1: When do Group 3 sustainability reporting obligations commence?
column2: Group 3 reporting obligations commence for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 1 July 2027.

column1: How long must a reporting entity retain its sustainability records after completing a sustainability report?
column2: Sustainability records must be retained for seven years after the relevant sustainability report is completed.

column1: What legal offense classification applies if an entity fails to keep required sustainability records?
column2: Failure to keep sustainability records is classified as a strict liability offense.

column1: Why does ASIC permit reporting entities to present integrated disclosures when voluntarily applying AASB S1 alongside AASB S2?
column2: Integrated disclosures prevent unnecessary duplication when governance and risk management are handled across sustainability topics holistically.

column1: Which Australian accounting standard sets out mandatory climate-related financial disclosure requirements?
column2: AASB S2 Climate-related Disclosures sets out these mandatory requirements.

column1: What constitutes Scope 3 Category 15 emissions for asset managers and banking institutions?
column2: Category 15 emissions consist of financed emissions associated with an entity's loans, investments, and financial activities.

column1: What consolidated gross assets threshold places a non-RSE corporate entity into Group 1 sustainability reporting?
column2: Consolidated gross assets equal to or greater than $1 billion place an entity in Group 1.

column1: Why must reporting entities use at least two distinct climate scenarios for climate resilience analysis?
column2: Two scenarios are required to evaluate resilience under both rapid near-term global decarbonisation and severe long-term physical climate impacts.

column1: What are the four core content pillars of climate disclosures required by AASB S2?
column2: The four core content pillars are governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics and targets.

column1: Why were modified liability settings introduced during the initial years of mandatory sustainability reporting?
column2: They were introduced to allow entities time to build mature reporting controls and capabilities without facing immediate litigation risk on complex disclosures.

column1: When do Group 2 sustainability reporting obligations commence?
column2: Group 2 reporting obligations commence for annual reporting periods beginning between 1 July 2026 and 30 June 2027.

column1: What location-based metric must be disclosed for Scope 2 emissions under AASB S2?
column2: Entities must disclose location-based Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions alongside relevant contractual instrument information.

column1: What constitutes a climate-related transition plan under AASB S2?
column2: A transition plan is an aspect of an entity's strategy laying out targets, actions, or resources for moving toward a lower-carbon economy.

column1: What temporary relief applies to Scope 3 emissions reporting in an entity's first year under AASB S2?
column2: Entities are exempt from disclosing Scope 3 emissions and comparative information during their first annual reporting period.

column1: What employee headcount threshold places a non-RSE corporate entity into Group 1 sustainability reporting?
column2: Having 500 or more employees at the end of the financial year places an entity in Group 1.

column1: What three core components comprise an entity's sustainability report under section 296A of the Corporations Act?
column2: A sustainability report consists of climate statements, notes to climate statements, and the directors' declaration.

column1: What defines Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions under AASB S2?
column2: Scope 1 emissions are direct greenhouse gas emissions from sources that are owned or controlled by the reporting entity.

column1: What consolidated revenue threshold places a non-RSE corporate entity into Group 1 sustainability reporting?
column2: Consolidated revenue equal to or greater than $500 million places an entity in Group 1.

column1: What must an entity disclose if it determines it has no material financial risks or opportunities relating to climate under section 296B(1)?
column2: It must lodge a statement declaring no material risks or opportunities exist and explain the process used to reach that conclusion.

column1: Why does the Corporations Act require sustainability reports to be provided to members alongside annual financial reports?
column2: This ensures members receive financial performance and climate-related risk disclosures concurrently to make fully informed decisions.

column1: What interaction exists between Operating and Financial Review requirements under section 299A and climate reporting?
column2: Listed entities must disclose climate risks in the Operating and Financial Review if reasonably required by members to assess operational and financial prospects.

column1: Why are small proprietary companies generally exempt from preparing a sustainability report?
column2: They are exempt because they are not required to prepare an annual financial report under Chapter 2M of the Corporations Act.

column1: Why does AASB S2 require disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated group and other investees?
column2: Disaggregation ensures users can distinguish direct group emissions from emissions of unconsolidated subsidiaries, joint ventures, and associates.

column1: What are climate-related transition risks?
column2: Transition risks are risks resulting from efforts to transition to a lower-carbon economy, including policy, legal, technological, market, and reputational risks.

column1: What executive remuneration disclosure is required under AASB S2 regarding climate considerations?
column2: Entities must disclose how climate considerations are factored into executive remuneration and the percentage of remuneration linked to climate factors.

column1: What is the primary objective of the risk management pillar in AASB S2?
column2: It enables users to understand how an entity identifies, assesses, prioritises, and monitors climate-related risks and opportunities.

column1: What are the threshold criteria for entities entering Group 3 sustainability reporting?
column2: Entities must meet two of three criteria: revenue of $50 million or more, gross assets of $25 million or more, or 100 or more employees.

column1: What administrative enforcement power does section 296E grant to ASIC regarding statements in a sustainability report?
column2: ASIC can direct an entity to substantiate, explain, complete, or correct any statement it considers incorrect, incomplete, or misleading.

column1: How is $CO_2$ equivalent defined in Appendix A of AASB S2?
column2: It is the universal unit measuring global warming potential of a greenhouse gas expressed relative to one unit of carbon dioxide.

column1: How does AASB S2 define chronic physical climate risks?
column2: Chronic physical risks arise from longer-term climatic shifts such as changes in precipitation, rising temperatures, and sea level rise.

column1: What modified liability protection applies to Scope 3 emissions and scenario analysis statements made between 2025 and 2027?
column2: Statements on Scope 3 emissions, scenario analysis, and transition plans are protected from private civil liability during this transition period.

column1: What defines Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions under AASB S2?
column2: Scope 2 emissions are indirect greenhouse gas emissions from the generation of purchased or acquired electricity, steam, heating, or cooling consumed by an entity.

column1: Why are reporting entities permitted to use reasonable and supportable information without undue cost or effort?
column2: This proportionality mechanism balances the need for useful disclosure with the entity's size, capabilities, and resource constraints.

column1: Which seven greenhouse gases recognized under the Kyoto Protocol are covered by AASB S2?
column2: The seven gases are carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride, and nitrogen trifluoride.

column1: Under what conditions may an entity omit quantitative disclosures of anticipated financial effects?
column2: Quantitative data may be omitted if effects are not separately identifiable, measurement uncertainty is excessively high, or the entity lacks required resources.

column1: What is an internal carbon price as defined in AASB S2?
column2: An internal carbon price is a value used by an entity to assess financial implications of potential emission abatement costs, risks, and decision-making trade-offs.

column1: What is the Group 1 reporting commencement timeframe for entities meeting the highest size or emissions thresholds?
column2: Group 1 reporting applies to annual reporting periods commencing between 1 January 2025 and 30 June 2026.

column1: How does AASB S2 define acute physical climate risks?
column2: Acute physical risks are event-driven risks arising from severe weather events such as storms, floods, droughts, or heatwaves.

column1: What is ASIC's primary regulatory role regarding sustainability reporting?
column2: ASIC supervises, administers, and enforces compliance to ensure market participants produce high-quality, decision-useful, and comparable disclosures.

column1: What is the statutory lodgement deadline for non-disclosing entities submitting sustainability reports to ASIC?
column2: Sustainability reports must be lodged within four months after the end of the financial year.

column1: What is the primary objective of the governance pillar in AASB S2?
column2: It enables users to understand the governance processes, controls, and procedures used to monitor, manage, and oversee climate-related risks and opportunities.

column1: When do full mandatory audit requirements for sustainability reports take effect in Australia?
column2: Full mandatory audit requirements take effect for financial reporting periods starting on or after 1 July 2030.

column1: What is the primary objective of the strategy pillar in AASB S2?
column2: It enables users to understand an entity's strategic approach to managing climate-related risks and opportunities over time.
